confirmed.summary: The deadly d6 the staff gains in Arcane Cascade is modelled nowhere, so the staff Strike's critical damage never picks up the extra die.
confirmed.printed: While you're in Arcane Cascade stance, your staff gains the deadly d6 trait, with the damage from the deadly die being the same damage type as the extra damage from Arcane Cascade.
confirmed.fix: The record's only fields are `critSpec: true` + `critSpecWeapons: { bases: ['staff'] }`, which cover the first sentence only (derive.ts:3281, weaponMatches at derive.ts:3393). Grepping `student-of-the-staff` across src/ returns zero hits — no situational star, no note, no mode. The lane exists: `weaponTraits` riders are collected from feats, class features AND active modes at derive.ts:3676-3684, merged by mergeTraits (derive.ts:3516) with deadly-family upgrade handling, and the deadly die is read into the crit rider at derive.ts:3878-3881. `cat-arcane-cascade` is already an active mode (modes.ts:258). Fix: author a mode gated `feats: ['student-of-the-staff']` (or extend the Arcane Cascade toggle) carrying `weaponTraits: { add: ['deadly-d6'], match: { items: ['staff'] } }`.

confirmed.summary: The barbarian's +10-foot Speed while raging is display-only — the record carries no mechanical field at all, so the Speed shown on the sheet never changes when the rage toggle is on.
confirmed.printed: While you are raging, you gain a +10-foot status bonus to your Speed.
confirmed.fix: core.json feats/fast-movement carries no field beyond name/level/traits; the only registry hit is the display star at situationalBonuses.ts:655, and that file's header says it is "DISPLAY-ONLY: nothing here changes a computed number". The lane for this exact shape exists and is used by nine records: `whileActive: [{ state: 'rage', speeds: {...} }]` (types.ts:1044-1051), gathered by activeStateGrants and pushed into grantSources at derive.ts:4428, then applied additively to land Speed at derive.ts:4481 (`if (key === 'land') speeds.land = (speeds.land ?? 0) + v`). raging-athlete uses `whileActive.speeds` and ligneous-instinct uses `whileActive.speedPenalty` for the mirror case. Fix: author `whileActive: [{ state: 'rage', speeds: { land: 10 } }]` on feats/fast-movement.

confirmed.summary: The feat is repeatable and the app lets you take it again, but the domain pick is stored once per RECORD, so every taking after the first grants no domain spell and no extra focus point.
confirmed.printed: **Special** You can select this feat multiple times, selecting a different domain each time and gaining its domain spell.
confirmed.fix: `maxTakable: null` → maxTakes() = Infinity (featGrants.ts:534-537), so the builder offers the feat again. But the domain answer lives at `build.effectChoices['blessing-of-the-sun-gods:domain']` — one key per (record, choiceId), read at build.ts:2979 and build.ts:4311. build.ts:4325-4328 documents this exact limitation ("a repeatable feat's takes all read the same `effectChoices[recordId:choiceId]` answer — so three takes of Wormskin printed 'Wormskin (Cold, Cold, Cold)'"), and build.ts:2977 iterates a Set of record ids, so the second take contributes nothing to `featFocusSpells`. Fix: move the domain pick off `effectChoices` onto the per-taking `choice` lane — `choice: { flag: 'domain', kind: 'domains', domainPool: [...] }`, which is keyed by SLOT via choiceKeys(slotKey, …) (build.ts:2874) and resolved per taking at build.ts:1510-1512.

confirmed.summary: The record's `spellcastingGrant` (divine / Charisma / trained) is never read for the focus entry, so the granted domain spell is cast as an occult spell keyed off the class's first key attribute — a Fighter Bright Lion rolls Dazzling Flash off Dexterity.
confirmed.printed: Your Bright Lion focus spells are divine spells; you become trained in divine spell attacks and spell DCs, using Charisma as your spellcasting ability score.
confirmed.fix: build.ts:3392 selects the feat casting profile with `.filter((f) => f?.spellcastingGrant && (f.focusSpells?.length || [f.spellcastingGrant].flat().some((g) => g?.focusOnly)))`. This record has no top-level `focusSpells` (its spell arrives through `effectChoices[].options[].grant.focusSpells`) and no `focusOnly`, so `featFocusGrant` is undefined and the chains at build.ts:3423-3424 fall through to `'occult'` and `focusCls.keyAbility[0]` (fighter → 'dex'; classes.fighter.keyAbility = ["dex","str"], no FOCUS_CASTING entry at build.ts:2478). bright-lion-dedication carries no spellcastingGrant either, so nothing else supplies it — the only other reader (build.ts:5193) applies these grants to the INNATE entry (build.ts:5950), which this feat never creates. Fix: set `focusOnly: true` on the record's spellcastingGrant, or widen the build.ts:3392 predicate to accept a record whose focus spell is granted through effectChoices. Seven sibling records share the shape (shadow-magic, perfect-ki-expert/-exemplar/-grandmaster, special-sentinel-technique, godling-dedication, holy-bloom).

confirmed.summary: The granted Detect Magic cantrip is written to a rank-0 `repertoire` slot that nothing renders on a prepared entry, and the write also flips the Hedge Mage archetype entry's Prepare modal into repertoire mode, hiding every prepared spell slot the character has.
confirmed.printed: Add the detect magic cantrip to your keepsake.
confirmed.fix: Record authors `spellListAdditions: { spells: ['detect-magic'], as: 'repertoire', entryId: 'hedge-mage-dedication-casting' }`. Detect Magic is rank 0, so build.ts:5537-5545 calls `addGrantedToRepertoire(archEntry, 0, 'detect-magic')` (build.ts:4707) on a PREPARED entry — hedge-mage-dedication is `mk('arcane','int',4,'hedge-mage')` with no `repertoire`, so build.ts:5514-5525 pushes `type: 'prepared'`. No reader: SpellsTab.tsx:1298 builds a main entry's cantrip cards from `main.cantrips` alone and SpellsTab.tsx:1338 renders only `main.prepared`; build.ts:5605-5608 already states in a comment that a rank-0 `grantedRepertoire` marker 'would be write-only'. Second consequence: SpellsTab.tsx:550 `const spontaneous = !!entry.repertoire` is now true, so SpellsTab.tsx:552 sets `ranks = Object.keys(entry.repertoire) = [0]` and the 'Prepare' button (SpellsTab.tsx:2041) opens a modal with no prepared ranks at all. Fix: for a prepared target entry push a rank-0 grant into `entry.cantrips` (the class path already unions `grantedByRank[0]` into cantrips at build.ts:3036), and change SpellsTab.tsx:550 to `entry.type === 'spontaneous'`.

confirmed.summary: Tremorsense is authored at a hard 5 feet with no level ladder, so a level 8+ character's sheet shows 5 feet when the printed text says 10 feet, and a level 12+ character's shows 5 feet instead of 15.
confirmed.printed: You gain darkvision and tremorsense as an imprecise sense within 5 feet. The range of the tremorsense increases to 10 feet at 8th level and to 15 feet at 12th level.
confirmed.fix: No lane exists: `SenseEntry` at src/rules/types.ts:435-446 carries only {name, range, acuity, superseded} — there is no level field anywhere in it, and the consumer at src/rules/derive.ts:2384 (`for (const s of src.senses ?? []) addSense(s)`) copies `range` verbatim. Add a ladder field (e.g. `rangeAt?: { level: number; range: number }[]`, highest step reached wins) to SenseEntry and resolve it inside addSense in deriveDefenses against `c.level`, then author `rangeAt: [{level:8,range:10},{level:12,range:15}]` on the tremorsense entry in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json (id `worm-sense`, field `senses`). Cheapest stopgap if the field is not wanted: a `note` on the record — but the displayed number stays wrong. Worm Caller Dedication is level 2, so a character holding this feat routinely reaches both breakpoints.

confirmed.summary: The Triple Time mode carries no modifiers at all, so a bard who toggles the composition this feat grants sees no change to their own Speed.
confirmed.printed: You learn the Triple Time composition cantrip, which speeds up you and your allies for a round.
confirmed.fix: The feat correctly grants the spell (`focusSpells: ['triple-time']`, and the spell is a cantrip with no `focus` trait so it rightly adds no Focus Point). The failure is the toggle: src/rules/modes.ts:234 is `{ id: 'cat-triple-time', ..., modifiers: [], note: 'Allies gain a +10-foot status bonus to their Speeds.' }`. The spell record itself reads "You and all allies in the area gain a +10-foot status bonus to all Speeds for 1 round", and its three siblings on the adjacent lines (cat-inspire-courage:231, cat-rallying-anthem:232, cat-song-of-strength:234-1) all apply their bonus to the character. The mode system already supports Speed — see `m(-10, 'untyped', 'speed')` on cat-wooden-rage (modes.ts:228) and the `{ kind: 'speed' }` target at modes.ts:29/87. Change modifiers to `[m(10, 'status', 'speed')]` and fix the note to "You and allies…".

confirmed.summary: The character receives four divine cantrips instead of two — two from the caster-archetype lane and two more as at-will innate spells from this record's own effectChoices.
confirmed.printed: You can prepare two common cantrips each day from the divine spell list or any other divine cantrips you have access to.
confirmed.fix: src/rules/casterArchetypes.ts:237-244 gives `red-mantis-assassin-dedication` `cantrips: 2`, and src/rules/build.ts:5466 builds the archetype entry with `cantrips: srcCantrips.slice(0, arch.config.cantrips + archCantripBonus)` — that alone delivers the two printed cantrips (activeCasterArchetype, casterArchetypes.ts:371, fires on the dedication). On top of that, scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:11145+ authors two `effectChoices` (`red-mantis-cantrip-1`, `red-mantis-cantrip-2`) with `spellFilter.grantAs: 'innate'`, `innate.atWill: true`, which the later effect-choice pass turns into two extra at-will innate divine cantrips (build.ts:5905-5926 innate/innateCantrips). Every other Basic-*-Spellcasting feat in core.json (basic-wizard/cleric/druid/bard-spellcasting) carries ZERO effectChoices for exactly this reason. Delete the two `effectChoices` entries for `basic-red-mantis-magic` from effect-backfill.json and let the casterArchetypes lane own the cantrips.

confirmed.summary: Animal Form is granted into the character's Focus-spell entry instead of the animist apparition repertoire, so it reads as a Focus-Point spell rather than something cast with apparition spellcasting.
confirmed.printed: You add Animal Form to your apparition spell repertoire, allowing you to cast it with your apparition spellcasting.
confirmed.fix: The record's `spellListAdditions` (scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:60278-60288, id `walk-the-wilds`) is `{ spells: ['animal-form'], as: 'repertoire' }` with NO `entryId`. The reader at src/rules/build.ts:4962-4963 does `const entry = entryId ? spellcasting.find(e => e.id === entryId) : spellcasting.find(e => e.type === 'focus') ?? spellcasting[0]` — an animist always has a focus entry (built at build.ts:3446 from the primary apparition's vessel spell), so Animal Form lands there, not in `animist-apparition-casting` (the spontaneous apparition pool built at build.ts:3160). The sibling feat proves the correct authoring: `monstrous-inclinations` prints the identical sentence and carries `"entryId": "animist-apparition-casting"`. Add the same `entryId` to walk-the-wilds' spellListAdditions in effect-backfill.json (and re-run `npm run data`).

confirmed.summary: The feat asks the domain question twice and can hand out two domain focus spells and two Focus Points where the printed text grants one, and the second question is not restricted to the three printed domains.
confirmed.printed: You gain the cleric's Domain Initiate feat but must select knowledge, secrecy, or truth as your domain. You cast that domain's domain spell as a focus spell of the same tradition as your cantrip from Eldritch Researcher Dedication
confirmed.fix: Two live lanes both grant. (1) core.json's effectChoices `domain` (authored at scripts/data/effect-backfill.json id `seeker-of-truths`, field `effectChoices`) offers knowledge/secrecy/truth, each option carrying `grant.focusSpells`; read by the effect-choice focus pass at src/rules/build.ts:2990-3001. (2) src/rules/featFeatGrants.ts:427 `'seeker-of-truths': ['domain-initiate']` makes the granted Domain Initiate's own `choice` (kind 'domains', domainPool 'deity') render its own picker at src/builder/Builder.tsx:2076 -> grantedChoicePicker (Builder.tsx:551, domains branch at :621), and answering it pushes DOMAIN_SPELLS[value] into featFocusSpells via applyFeatFocus (build.ts:2826-2830, called for granted feats at build.ts:2963). poolMax counts distinct focus spells (build.ts:3339 + the 'FOCUS POOL = THE NUMBER OF FOCUS SPELLS YOU KNOW' block at build.ts:3530), so two spells = two points. There is no FEAT_GRANT_BOUND_CHOICE entry binding domain-initiate to seeker-of-truths (checked src/rules/featFeatGrants.ts:285 isBoundGrant and the FEAT_GRANT_BOUND_CHOICE table), and the `kind: 'domains'` branch in Builder.tsx:621 bypasses narrowChoiceOptions entirely, so the second picker also offers the whole deity list rather than knowledge/secrecy/truth. Fix: add `'seeker-of-truths': { 'domain-initiate': ... }` to FEAT_GRANT_BOUND_CHOICE so the granted feat's domain answer is taken from the Seeker of Truths effectChoice (the same shape already used for Weight of Experience -> Assurance), leaving exactly one question and one focus spell.

confirmed.summary: The feat's second printed sentence — a +1 to the extra Rage damage on repertoire spells while Drained — has no entry anywhere, even though the identical clause on its own level-12 successor does.
confirmed.printed: "In addition, when you Cast a Spell from your repertoire and you are at least Drained 1, increase the extra damage dealt by that spell from Rage by 1."
confirmed.fix: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts FEAT_SITUATIONAL — add `"rising-blood-magic": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'spellDamage' }], when: "raging repertoire spell while Drained 1+", bonus: "+1" }]`. The lane and reader already exist and are already used for the very next tier: line 2894 carries `"surging-blood-magic": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'spellDamage' }], when: "raging repertoire spell while Drained 2+ (Rising Blood Magic)", bonus: "+2 (total 3)" }]` — that entry's own `when` names Rising Blood Magic as the base it stacks onto, but the base itself was never authored. Grep confirms `rising-blood-magic` appears in src/ only at src/rules/casterArchetypes.ts:155 (as bloodrager-dedication's basicId, which handles only the spell-slot half of the feat).

confirmed.summary: The Daydream Trance toggle the feat grants is registered in CATALOG_MODES with an empty `modifiers` array and a note that carries none of the printed numbers, so switching it on changes nothing on the sheet.
confirmed.printed: "You can send yourself into a half-awake, daydreaming state and gain the Daydream Trance action." — and the granted action (core.json actions['daydream-trance'], aonParentId feat-8515) prints: "You gain a +1 status bonus to Will saves. This bonus increases to +2 against mental effects. If you're legendary in Occultism, the bonus against mental effects increases to +3. You take a -1 penalty to Perception checks and initiative rolls."
confirmed.fix: src/rules/modes.ts:340 `{ id: 'cat-daydream-trance', … modifiers: [], note: 'Sleepwalker (Dark Archive): enter a daydream trance.' }` — author the modifiers: m(1,'status','save',{detail:'will'}), a second save entry with appliesWhen 'against mental effects (+3 if you are legendary in Occultism)', m(-1,'untyped','perception') and m(-1,'untyped','initiative'), and restate the numbers in `note`. Every target kind is already in ModeTargetKind (src/rules/types.ts:3629) and read: saves at src/rules/derive.ts:221 (modeTypedMods), Perception at src/rules/derive.ts:345, initiative at src/rules/initiative.ts:43. modes.ts:287 already names this exact shape as a defect — "`modifiers: []` and no `battleForm` — prose pretending to be a toggle" — and RAW_MODES' own header rule says a clean numeric bonus must be encoded as a modifier and a non-numeric one must at least be spelled out in the note; this entry does neither.

confirmed.summary: The second and third takes of Wormskin grant no resistance at all — every take reads the same stored answer, so a player who spends three feats gets one damage type instead of three.
confirmed.printed: "**Special** You can take this feat up to three times, each time selecting a new damage type from the list." (record carries maxTakable: 3)
confirmed.fix: The picker that actually grants is `effectChoices[resistance]`, whose answer is stored under build.effectChoices[`${recordId}:${ch.id}`] — one key for the whole record, not per take (written at src/builder/Builder.tsx:2090, read at src/rules/build.ts:4310). The codebase already documents this at src/rules/build.ts:4322-4325 ("a repeatable feat's takes all read the same effectChoices[recordId:choiceId] answer — so three takes of Wormskin printed 'Wormskin (Cold, Cold, Cold)'") but only the duplicated LABEL was fixed, not the shared grant. The per-take carrier is the record's own `choice`: answers are keyed by slotKey (choiceKeys(), src/rules/build.ts:471) and `choice.options[].grant` is applied once per feat instance at src/rules/build.ts:4529-4533. Move the three `grant.resistances` onto choice.options[].grant, delete the effectChoices block, and set distinctAcrossTakes (types.ts:2361) so the three takes must differ.

confirmed.summary: The sheet shows the swashbuckler's SCALING Precise Strike damage to a character whose feat text explicitly freezes that damage, so the strike-damage star list states a number the feat forbids.
confirmed.printed: "You gain the Precise Strike class feature but you deal 1 addition damage on a hit and 1d6 damage on a finisher. This damage doesn't increase as you gain levels."
confirmed.fix: core.json feats/finishing-precision carries grantsClassFeatures:['precise-strike'] and nothing that caps it. That id enters ownedFeatureIds (src/rules/derive.ts:3088), which characterSituationalIds pulls in (src/rules/explain.ts:242), which resolves FEAT_SITUATIONAL['precise-strike'] (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2978 — "+2 precision (+1 more at 5th, 9th, 13th, 17th); 2d6 precision instead if the Strike is a finisher (+1d6 at those levels)"). It renders beside the correct FEAT_SITUATIONAL['finishing-precision'] line (situationalBonuses.ts:2758, "+1 precision"), so the strike-damage popup carries two contradictory rows. Needs the Precise Strike twin of `precisionDice` (src/rules/types.ts:1028, which exists for exactly this shape on Sneak Attack): a non-scaling override authored on finishing-precision, read where featSituationalLines() builds the strikeDamage list (src/rules/explain.ts:707) so the granted feature's own line is replaced rather than added.

confirmed.summary: The builder asks the same damage-type question twice; the answer to the record's own `choice` (flag "damage") changes no number and reaches nothing.
confirmed.printed: "You gain resistance equal to half your level versus one of the following types of damage, chosen when you take the feat: fire, cold, or bludgeoning."
confirmed.fix: core.json feats/wormskin has BOTH `choice` {flag:'damage', options bludgeoning/cold/fire} and `effectChoices[resistance]` with the identical option set; only the effectChoices options carry `grant`. Nothing reads the `choice`: the only src/ reference to the id is src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3078 (the unarmored-AC line, which reads `unarmoredAc` at src/rules/derive.ts:1723, not the choice), and no record uses fromChoiceFlag/weaponFromChoiceFlag 'damage' (0 hits in core.json). This is precisely the "(a) ASKED TWICE" family the PHANTOM table in scripts/apply-builder-choice-sets.mjs:86-96 exists to delete, and wormskin is missing from it — one of 18 records still carrying identical duplicate option sets. Either add it to PHANTOM, or (preferred, and it also fixes the multi-take defect above) keep the `choice`, move the grants onto it, and delete the effectChoices.

confirmed.summary: A necromancer with this feat sees nothing on their Harm spell saying its 3-action area can be extended — the record carries no mechanical field of any kind.
confirmed.printed: "Whenever you cast the 3-action version of harm, you can extend the area to a 60-foot emanation."
confirmed.fix: core.json feats/overwhelming-harm has only identity fields (id/name/traits/rarity/source/level/category/edition/aonId) — no spellNotes, no note, no mode, and no entry in any src/rules registry (grep of the id across src/ returns zero hits). The built lane for exactly this sentence shape is `spellNotes` (88 entries shipped): authored on the record, collected at src/rules/build.ts:4878, exposed as Character.spellNotes and read by spellNotesFor() at src/rules/explain.ts:667. Cruelty, in this same batch, carries spellNotes for touch-of-the-void for the identical "when you cast X you may…" shape. Author spellNotes: [{ spellId: 'harm', note: '…extend the area of the 3-action version to a 60-foot emanation.' }].

confirmed.summary: Only the Perception half of the feat is registered; the +1 circumstance bonus to Deception/Diplomacy/Intimidation/Performance against a creature you caught lying is in no lane, so those four skills carry no star.
confirmed.printed: "When you determine someone is lying to you, you can use their deceit to your advantage to gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the next Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, or Performance check you attempt against that creature within the next minute."
confirmed.fix: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:359 currently holds a single clause — `"lie-detector": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'perception' }], when: "Perception to Sense Motive, and DC vs attempts to Lie to you", bonus: "+1 circumstance" }]`. Append a second SituationalBonus with `targets: [{kind:'skill',detail:'deception'},{kind:'skill',detail:'diplomacy'},{kind:'skill',detail:'intimidation'},{kind:'skill',detail:'performance'}]`, when "vs a creature you determined was lying, for 1 minute (or +1 to your Pursue a Lead bonus instead, if it applies)", bonus "+1 circumstance". Read by modeTypedMods' sibling skill-star path — skill situational targets surface at src/rules/derive.ts:507 / the skill detail popup, the same route the existing perception clause already takes.

confirmed.summary: The printed lock on raising Folktales Lore is not in LOCKED_SKILL_KEYS, so a player can still spend an ordinary skill increase on it — the exact thing the sentence forbids, and the thing the identical Bardic Lore clause is already guarded against.
confirmed.printed: "If you are legendary in the Performance skill, you gain expert proficiency in Folktales Lore, but you can't increase your proficiency rank in Folktales Lore by any other means."
confirmed.fix: src/rules/featGrants.ts:525 `LOCKED_SKILL_KEYS` contains exactly one key, `'lore:bardic'`. Add `'lore:folktales'` with the equivalent message. Two readers already consume it: src/rules/build.ts:2685 (`if (LOCKED_SKILL_KEYS[key]) continue;` in the skill-increase loop) and src/builder/Builder.tsx:2209/2215 (disables the increase button and shows the reason). The trained grant and the Performance-gated expert step are already correct in src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts:253-255 via `crossConditionalSkills`, read at src/rules/build.ts:4112 — only the lock half is missing. (featGrantsAuto.ts:82-85 documents that Bardic Lore needed BOTH halves for the same sentence.)

confirmed.summary: The record asks the player to choose one of two benefits, but neither option carries a grant, so the answer changes nothing — and the spontaneous branch's two extra signature repertoire spells are never delivered.
confirmed.printed: If you're a spontaneous spellcaster with the signature spells class feature, add two of the spells from the list of sacred spells to your repertoire. They are signature spells for you, in addition to your normal signature spells.
confirmed.fix: The 7-spell list access works (`spellListAdditions`, read at src/rules/build.ts:4726-4762 into `character.spellListAdditions`, consumed by src/sheet/SpellsTab.tsx:286-287). The `choice` authored at scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:67177 (`flag: 'sacredSpellsBenefit'`) has two options, neither with a `grant` and with no `inert` explanation; grepping `sacredSpellsBenefit` across src/ returns zero hits, and a `choice` answer can only do something through `options[].grant` (FeatChoiceDef, src/rules/types.ts:2284). The spontaneous branch needs two picks of the seven that land in the repertoire and in `SpellcastingEntry.signatureFixed` (src/rules/types.ts:4477) — note `EffectChoice.spellFilter.grantAs` currently only supports 'innate' | 'focus' | 'staff' (types.ts:1842), so either extend it with a repertoire/signature shape or author the pick as a two-pick choice whose options carry a repertoire grant. At minimum, if the pick is to stay recorded-only, give it `inert` so the player is told the answer grants nothing.

confirmed.summary: The passive dedication carries actionCost {type:'reaction'} inherited from its embedded Spirit's Mercy sub-block, which already ships as its own action record, so the player is offered the same reaction twice — once under the dedication's name with no trigger and no cost line.
confirmed.printed: You've learned to attract, quell, and purify spirits... Any actions you gain from the exorcist archetype gain either the divine or occult trait... Spirit's Mercy is the simplest of the purifications.
confirmed.fix: Set `actionCost: {"type":"passive"}` on the feat (scripts/data/effect-backfill.json, category `feats`, id `exorcist-dedication`, field `actionCost`). Evidence the reaction belongs to the child, not the parent: core.json `actions['spirits-mercy']` carries actionCost {type:'reaction'}, `aonParentId: "feat-3454"` and `aonSection: "Spirit's Mercy"` — i.e. the scraper split the sub-activity out but the parent kept the child's badge — and the feat already grants it via `grantsActions: ["spirits-mercy"]`. The consequence: src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:278 `.filter((f) => !!f && isActionCost(f.actionCost) && !activityNames.has(f.name))` accepts 'reaction', and the dedupe on line 279 is by NAME, so both "Exorcist Dedication" and "Spirit's Mercy" land in featActions. AoN feat-3454 carries no `actions`/`action_type` field at all — weak on its own per the project's badge ruling (a bare badge is scrape damage), but corroborating here. Flagged medium because this shape is systemic: 37 dedications in core.json carry a non-passive actionCost, including firework-technician-dedication (1 action, matching its granted launch-fireworks), so it may be a known accepted state rather than a per-record slip.

confirmed.summary: Nothing on the sheet surfaces that the rogue's sneak attack can ride a damaging spell attack — the record carries no field and appears in no registry, so the clause lives only in the feat's prose.
confirmed.printed: When you succeed at a spell attack roll against an off-guard foe's AC and the spell deals damage, you can add your sneak attack damage to the damage roll.
confirmed.fix: core.json feats/magical-trickster has only `actionCost: { type: 'passive' }`; grep of `magical-trickster` across src/ returns zero hits. situationalBonuses.ts declares a `spellDamage` target kind for exactly this shape (situationalBonuses.ts, SituationalTarget union — deliberately prose-only, "every entry renders a 'when' the player reads and applies themselves"), and the analogous rogue clause is already authored that way for sly-striker (situationalBonuses.ts:2891, `kind: 'strikeDamage'`). Fix: add `"magical-trickster": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'spellDamage' }], when: "on a successful spell attack roll against an off-guard foe, when the spell deals damage (once per target)", bonus: "+ your sneak attack damage" }]` to FEAT_SITUATIONAL, which reaches the Spells/stat detail popups through featSituationalLines (explain.ts:707) and characterSituationalIds (explain.ts:238).

rejected.summary: The player is asked three questions for two terrains, only one Terrain Stalker is actually granted, and the two answers on Terrain Scout itself drive nothing but a label.
why:
REFUTED. The claim's three load-bearing assertions each fail against the code.

1. "The two terrainScoutTerrains answers are read by nothing mechanical." False. Three readers, none of them a label:
   - src/rules/build.ts:862 — `const picked = choiceKeys(key, feat.choice).every((k) => build.featChoices?.[k]);` gates `levelChoices`. Because `choiceKeys` fans a picks:2 choice out to `<slotKey>#0`/`#1`, the level carries a required "Terrain Scout — choose" entry until BOTH terrains are answered, and the Create/Save completeness check that reads levelChoices cannot reach zero. That is validation, not a row label.
   - src/rules/build.ts:2874-2884 — the multi-pick resolve/join lane, whose own comment names this exact record: "A multi-pick choice ('choose two different terrains') stores one answer per index; resolve each and show them joined, so the feat row reads 'Terrain Scout (Forest, Swamp)' rather than naming only the first." It writes `featChoiceById[slotKey] = { value: values.join(','), label: labels.join(', ') }`. The lane was built FOR terrain-scout.
   - src/rules/build.ts:504 (`choiceOptionsFor`, `if (!def?.distinct) return options;`), reached from src/builder/Builder.tsx:500 — `distinct: true` removes pick 1's answer from pick 2's list. That IS the printed clause "choosing a different terrain each time", enforced. The claim never mentions that the printed constraint is honoured.
   The claim's `choiceAnswersById` finding (build.ts:4715-4716 serving only spellListAdditions) is true but is one lane of several, and is not the lane a multi-pick record travels.

2. "The answers drive nothing but a label" is not a defect here — it is this project's own ruled-correct outcome. Terrain Stalker changes no number: core.json's two `situational` entries are "Sneak without attempting a Stealth check" and "automatically approach within 15 feet". No answer can move a number that does not exist. scripts/builder-evidence.mjs:806-808 states the rule verbatim: "`echo-only` IS NOT THE SAME FAILURE AS `not-read`… for a feat whose whole job is to record WHICH skill, that label is the correct and complete surface (Ruling K…). `not-read` is stronger… only one of them is automatically wrong." I ran the project's own instrument: `npx jiti scripts/builder-evidence.mjs --only terrain-scout` → `pickers rendered 3`, `by lane {"choice":2,"grantedFeatChoice":1}`, `answer verdicts {"echo-only":3}`, `nothing moves at all 0`. Zero not-read.

3. "Only one Terrain Stalker is granted" is a shape difference, not a lost mechanic. FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS['terrain-scout'] (featFeatGrants.ts:457) is read at build.ts:3956 (`featFeatGrantsFor`) and pushed at build.ts:3978, so the Terrain Stalker row mounts and carries its Stealth situational stars. A second row would add exactly one thing over the shipped shape: a second terrain STRING — which terrain-scout's own picks:2/distinct choice already stores, cross-excludes, and prints on the Feats-tab row (src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:112). No number, prerequisite, star, action or focus point differs between the two shapes.

4. "The ruling was already written and not applied." work/choice-lane/corrections.json is a review of a SPEC, and its stated blocker is now stale: it argues the choice must be dropped because "the `choice` shape holds ONE value (build.ts:3251 …), so picks:2 has nowhere to live." `choiceKeys` (build.ts:471) gives it somewhere to live, and build.ts:2874-2884 joins the labels. The engine took the other branch deliberately and locked it under test — test/bespoke-tail.test.ts:105-110 ("Terrain Scout asks for BOTH terrains", asserting picks===2 and distinct===true) and test/builder-evidence.test.ts:107-113 ("picks:2 renders TWO pickers under one prompt", asserting p[0].key !== p[1].key). Citing an unapplied spec correction as the ruling ignores the branch that shipped with tests behind it.

5. "The record's own note … is implemented by nothing." Category error. src/builder/Builder.tsx:516-520 renders `def.note` immediately beneath the two pickers, under the comment "A restriction the app cannot enforce — name the part that is on the player, instead of silently offering a wider list than the rules allow." builder-evidence.mjs:818-820 says the same: "A `note` is the app telling the player which part of the restriction is theirs to honour." A note is not a promise of automation.

Residual, and it is not the claimed defect: the granted Terrain Stalker row does mount its own picker (Builder.tsx:2076 → grantedChoicePicker, Builder.tsx:551), so three controls render. It is echo-only like the other two, it is explained in place by the note, and it costs the player no number, no star and no prerequisite. Cosmetic redundancy at most — not "the player gets nothing", not "a field read by nothing", and not grounds to rewrite a lane that ships under two tests.

rejected.summary: The entire benefit is invisible on the Summon Instrument spell; the record carries only a bare "1/turn" use pip whose meaning appears nowhere.
why:
REFUTED. The claim's headline ("the meaning appears nowhere") is false, and its proposed fix is display polish outside its own lane.

1) The one character-sheet mechanic IS built and read. `limitedUses {max:1, per:'turn'}` is read by `featUse()` at src/rules/featUses.ts:83 and rendered as spend/restore pips at src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:427-470, on the row bearing the feat's own name (aria-label={`Spend a use of ${use.name}`}), with a literal "per turn" label and the sub-daily "New encounter" refill control (isSubDaily, src/rules/featUses.ts:105). That row opens FeatDetail (src/sheet/FeatDetail.tsx:114), which renders the full printed text via DescBody. The pip is attached to the named feat whose text sits one click away in the same list — not floating meaningless.

2) Nothing else printed is character-sheet-shaped. "modify its duration to be sustained, up to 1 minute" and "a number of instruments equal to your spellcasting ability modifier" are per-cast prose off a modifier the sheet already shows. "on a failure, it becomes distracted... and becomes off-guard for 1 round. The target is then temporarily immune for 24 hours" lands on an OPPONENT — and no lane for inflicting a condition on a target exists anywhere in the app (grep -rn "inflictsCondition|targetCondition|appliesCondition" src/ returns zero hits). The save is "against the spell's DC", i.e. the character's own spell DC, already derived and displayed. Per the rubric these are prose/GM-facing clauses with no character-sheet consequence.

3) The proposed spellNotes fix is out of lane. Of the 76 feats in public/core.json carrying spellNotes, 71 annotate a spell the record ITSELF grants (innateSpells/focusSpells/grantsRituals). The five exceptions (Mercy, Cruelty, Vellumis Excision + the two answer-driven shapes fromChoice/fromCantripPick) all modify a spell a CLASS FEATURE guarantees is present. Summon Ensemble grants nothing and its prerequisite ("ability to cast summon instrument") is unverified by the app. All six sibling Spell Trickster feats — agile-hand, barrier-shield, forceful-push, shining-arms, tracing-sigil, wild-lights — likewise carry no spellNotes; this is the archetype's consistent shape, not a one-record oversight.

Registry check confirming ourRegistries: []: grep -rn "summon-ensemble" over src/**/*.{ts,tsx} and scripts/**/*.{ts,tsx,mjs} returns nothing; the only hits anywhere are scripts/data/effect-backfill.json entry 3428 (the limitedUses author, so it survives `npm run data`) and entry 1406 (its listing as a spell-trickster-dedication pick option). featGrants*/featPickGrants/featFeatGrants/featCantripGrants/companionGrants/situationalBonuses/featUses/domains/modes.ts CATALOG_MODES/casterArchetypes.ts all name it nowhere — correctly, since it needs none of them.

A cross-reference note on the Summon Instrument entry would be a nice enhancement, but the benefit is already visible on the feat the player owns, and the only trackable number is authored and read. Not a defect.

rejected.summary: The feat may be taken twice and each taking asks its own tradition question, but the spell picker resolves the flag by first-answer-wins, so the second taking's answer is discarded and its spells are filtered to the first taking's tradition — the opposite of what the Special clause requires.
why:
REFUTED — the claim misreads the code, and its fix would create a defect rather than remove one.

1) The printed constraint IS built and read. core.json's `esoteric-spellcasting` carries `choice.flag: "esotericSpellcastingTradition"` plus `traditionFromChoiceFlag: "esotericSpellcastingTradition"` on all three `effectChoices[].spellFilter`s. `narrowSpellFilter` (src/rules/build.ts:1475) has four live readers: src/builder/Builder.tsx:2096 and src/builder/shared.tsx:4136 (the pickers) and src/rules/build.ts:2994 and src/rules/build.ts:4316 (the engine that actually builds the innate grant). The "spells of the same tradition you chose" clause therefore reaches the sheet.

2) The claim's premise — that the second taking has "its own three effectChoices spell pickers" whose answers are discarded — is false. `effectChoices` answers are keyed by RECORD ID, never by slot:
   · src/builder/Builder.tsx:2091 — `const ecKey = `${picked}:${ch.id}``
   · src/rules/build.ts:4310 — `const val = build.effectChoices?.[`${recordId}:${ch.id}`]`
   · src/rules/build.ts:2980 — same key shape in the focus pass
   · src/rules/build.ts:4475 — `for (const fc of feats) resolvePick(fc.featId, …)` runs once per TAKING but reads that same record-global key
This is deliberate and documented at src/rules/build.ts:4321-4325: "a repeatable feat's takes all read the same effectChoices[recordId:choiceId] answer" (the comment cites Wormskin printing "(Cold, Cold, Cold)"). The repo knows how to slot-key a repeatable feat's sub-answers where it wants that (Builder.tsx:2014-2018 and build.ts:4226-4229 do exactly that for Lore) and did not here. So both takings render the SAME three controls bound to the SAME three keys — there is no separate "second taking's spells" that could be filtered to the wrong tradition. First-answer-wins is the only coherent resolution of one shared answer.

3) The proposed fix would actively break things. Threading a slot key into `narrowSpellFilter` would make the identical `ecKey` render under occult in slot A and divine in slot B, so one stored spell id would appear valid in one slot and missing in the other. And the two ENGINE call sites (build.ts:2994, build.ts:4316) iterate effectChoices keys and owned records — they have no slot context and structurally cannot acquire one — so the sheet would still resolve a single tradition while the builder showed two. That is the "correct data behind a reader that never looks" failure this codebase repeatedly hits.

A separate and different observation is true — because the answer keys are record-global, a second taking yields no ADDITIONAL spells — but that lives in the effectChoices key design, not in narrowSpellFilter, and the proposed fix does not address it. As stated, the claimed defect and its fix are wrong.

rejected.summary: The clause that halves your kineticist level for this impulse is nowhere on the record, while the impulse the feat grants displays its own un-halved scaling line — so the app shows an archetype user a range and Bulk the feat explicitly contradicts.
why:
REFUTED — the claim's two load-bearing assertions are both false, and the third ("a number that disagrees with the printed text") has no number to disagree with.

1. "The clause ... is nowhere on the record" is wrong. It IS the record — it is the feat's entire printed description, and that description is live, rendered content, not inert data. `public/core-descriptions.json` → `feats['base-kinesis'].d` = "You gain the Base Kinesis impulse. For the purposes of determining when the range and Bulk improvements of the action occur, your kineticist level is equal to half your level (for example, ... 45 feet and could affect 1 Bulk ...)". READER: `C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/data/index.ts:514-548` fetches core-descriptions.json and writes each `d` back onto the record, and `C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:106` (`for (const fc of character.feats)`) → line 116 `description: withPicks(fc.featId, feat.description)` puts that exact sentence on the Feats tab row for every character who took the feat, plus the FeatDetail popup. The player is told the rule verbatim, in the app, on the record itself. The claim silently equates "no mechanical field" with "nowhere on the record".

2. "The app shows an archetype user a range and Bulk the feat explicitly contradicts" is wrong — the app shows no range and no Bulk. `public/core.json` `classFeatures['base-kinesis']` and `actions['base-kinesis']` carry NO `range` and NO bulk field (fields present: id, name, traits, rarity, source, level, actionCost, edition, aonId). And there is no "Level (+N)" engine anywhere: `grep -rn "Level (+" src/` returns zero hits. 66 records across core-descriptions.json carry a `**Level (+N)**` scaling line (60 feats, 3 actions, 2 classFeatures, 1 class) and the app level-substitutes none of them for anyone. The "un-halved scaling line" the claim objects to is simply the impulse's own printed prose, byte-identical to Rage of Elements and AoN, shown identically to a real kineticist (for whom it is correct). Two blocks of printed prose sitting next to each other exactly as the rulebook prints them is not a contradiction the app manufactured, and there is no derived value for the halved level to correct.

3. The mechanic is otherwise correctly wired. `derive.ts:3088` reads `grantsClassFeatures` and adds `base-kinesis` to `ownedFeatureIds`; `MainTab.tsx:238-240` pulls `ownedFeatureIds` into `actionRecords` and line 277 builds `featActions`, so the archetype user actually receives the 2-action impulse on their action list. Nothing is withheld.

4. What the clause actually governs — when the range/Bulk steps occur — is an out-of-combat utility adjudication the printed text itself hands to the table ("The GM decides what Bulk the element is"). It touches no stat, no DC, no strike, no defence, and no field the sheet computes.

The proposed `RECORD_MARKERS['base-kinesis'] = [{ on: 'feature', ... }]` would also be the wrong instrument even if a marker were wanted: `recordMarkersFor(character, content, 'feature', recordId)` in FeatsTab.tsx:99 is called only from the entry loops, and for a non-kineticist the granted impulse is never pushed as a `feature` row (FeatsTab's feature loops walk `cls.features`, subclass `featureIds`, classChoices, inventor mods, grantedFeatures and heritages — not `ownedFeatureIds`), so an `on: 'feature'` mark on `base-kinesis` would render for nobody. It would be a new instance of the exact write-only-without-a-reader defect the brief warns about. The only lane that would actually display is `modifiesGrant.actionRider` (read at `src/rules/build.ts:4677-4686`, keyed to MainTab.tsx:624), which is already used against this same action by `extended-kinesis` in `scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:115249`. That is at most an optional convenience restating text already on the sheet — not a missing mechanic, and not what was claimed.

rejected.summary: The archetype's "same tradition as your other spells" clause never fires for this focus spell, so an archetype-caster taker casts it off a fallback occult/Strength profile.
why:
REFUTED — measured on built characters, not read off the source.

WHAT THE RECORD PRINTS IS DELIVERED. `magic-warrior-aspect` prints exactly one mechanic: "You gain the Magic Warrior Aspect focus spell." The record carries `focusSpells: ["magic-warrior-aspect"]` (public/core.json), which is read at C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\build.ts:2833 (`const ffs = (feat.focusSpells ?? []).filter(...)`) into `featFocusSpells`, folded into `focusSpells` at build.ts:3340-3346, and pushed into the focus entry's `repertoire` at build.ts:3446-3463. The spell carries the `focus` trait, so it also counts toward `poolMax` (build.ts:3498-3500). Measured: on every build I made the spell is in the focus repertoire. Nothing this record prints is missing.

THE CLAUSE THE CLAIM INVOKES IS PRINTED ON A DIFFERENT RECORD, AND IT HAS A FIELD AND A READER. "Your focus spells from the magic warrior archetype are the same tradition as your other spells (choose one if you have spells from multiple traditions)" is the last sentence of `magic-warrior-dedication`'s description (public/core-descriptions.json), not of the aspect. That record does carry `focusFromSpellSlots: true` — authored at scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:135986-135990 — and the flag has a live reader at src/rules/build.ts:5571-5583, with a regression test already asserting it (test/batch10-parity.test.ts:20-21).

THE NAMED FAILING CASE IS NOT A LEGAL CHARACTER. The claim's scenario is "a fighter with, say, Wizard Dedication plus Magic Warrior". Magic Warrior Dedication's printed prerequisite is "ability to cast focus spells" (public/core.json). Wizard Dedication + Basic Wizard Spellcasting grant spell SLOTS, no focus spells — that fighter cannot legally take the dedication at all. (The builder does not block it, because `checkPrerequisites` at build.ts:7445 only enforces declared tokens, ability lines, rank lines and known feat ids; a prose line like "ability to cast focus spells" falls through by design. That under-enforcement, if anyone cares, is a prerequisite-gating gap — not a data defect on this feat.)

THE PROPOSED FIX IS A NO-OP FOR EVERY CHARACTER WHO LEGALLY QUALIFIES. I ran it. Setting `focusFromSpellSlots: true` on the aspect/transformation and rebuilding:
  fighter + wizard ded (illegal — no focus spells) : occult/dex -> arcane/int   (the ONLY case that changes)
  druid + magic warrior (legal)                    : primal/wis -> primal/wis   (unchanged)
  champion + wizard ded + magic warrior (legal)    : divine/cha -> divine/cha   (unchanged)
The reason is the deliberate guard at build.ts:5578-5581 — `held.every((id) => borrowIds.has(id))`, documented three lines above as "Retarget only when every focus spell in the entry came from such a record… moving it would relabel the class's spells to satisfy the archetype's clause, which is the wrong way round." Because the dedication's own prerequisite forces a legal taker to already own focus spells, the entry can never be all-magic-warrior, so the lane is correctly inert for them either way.

AND THE ANSWER THE APP GIVES A LEGAL TAKER IS RIGHT. A qualifying character's focus spells ARE some of "your other spells", so the entry's tradition is always one of that character's own traditions: druid gets primal/Wis (their only tradition — exactly the printed sentence); champion + Wizard Dedication gets divine/Cha, which the printed "choose one if you have spells from multiple traditions" explicitly permits. No number on the sheet disagrees with the printed text for any character who can actually take the feat.

So the claim misattributes a clause from `magic-warrior-dedication` to `magic-warrior-aspect`, and its only reproducible symptom requires a build that violates that dedication's printed prerequisite. Sending someone to edit effect-backfill.json here would change nothing for any legal character.

rejected.summary: The resistance is authored unqualified, so the character resists ALL spirit and void damage equal to their level, when the printed text limits it to damage from a haunt, spirit, or incorporeal undead.
why:
REFUTED — the record is fine, and the proposed fix would break it.

1. THE MECHANIC IS BUILT, WITH NAMED READERS. `src/rules/derive.ts:2259-2262` (`for (const f of c.feats) { const feat = db.feats[f.featId]; if (feat) push(feat.name ?? f.featId, feat); }`) pushes the feat's `resistances` into the defense sources. `derive.ts:2400` resolves `"@actor.level"` through `resolveFormula`, `derive.ts:2413` does `res.set(r.type, Math.max(...))`, `derive.ts:2577` emits `resistances: [...res].map(([type, value]) => ({ type, value }))`, and `src/sheet/DefensesPills.tsx:52` and `src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:774` render the pills with the breakdown. A level-4 campfire chronicler receives Spirit 4 / Void 4 with "The Dead Tell Tales" named as the source. I confirmed the built record in `public/core.json` (feats/the-dead-tell-tales) carries both entries.

2. THE PROPOSED FIX IS AFFIRMATIVELY HARMFUL, AND THE CODEBASE ALREADY RULED ON IT. `src/rules/types.ts:491-495` states verbatim: "⚠ NOT the same as `against`. An `against` entry is deliberately withheld from the computed total, and both IWR surfaces iterate the resolved resistances — so a type whose ONLY contributor is `against` renders on no screen at all. That is why no record uses it." I verified the whole path: `derive.ts:2405-2407` `continue`s BEFORE `res.set`, so an `against` entry never enters `res`; `derive.ts:2577` builds the exposed `resistances` array only from `res`; and EVERY consumer of `def.sources` is keyed off a type that must already exist in that resolved list — `explain.ts:1456` (`defenses.sources?.[`${kind}:${type}`]`), `DefensesPills.tsx:52/64/76`, `VitalsRail.tsx:774/790/806`, and the HP damage chips at `VitalsRail.tsx:1234` (`resistances={...charDefenses.resistances}`). Spirit and void have no other contributor on a campfire chronicler, so adding `against` to both rows would remove the feat's only mechanical effect from every screen in the app. The player would get NOTHING. The note written at `derive.ts:2406` would be permanently unreachable — the codebase's signature "field with no reader" defect, created on purpose by the fix.

3. THE CLAIM'S MEASUREMENT IS INVERTED. I re-measured `public/core.json` directly: 254 resistance entries; exactly 1 uses `against` (`modes/dampening-harmonics`, type "all"); exactly 1 uses `condition` (`feats/stoney-skin`, "except adamantine"). The claim reads "only ONE of 254 uses `against`, so this record's over-grant is the norm this lane was built to fix." The types.ts comment says the opposite: the near-zero count is the DESIGNED state ("That is why no record uses it"), not a backlog. `against` is reserved for a qualifier that should be withheld AND whose type has another contributor to hang the line on; the counted-but-annotated lane for a limit the sheet cannot check is `condition`.

4. THE PRINTED LIMIT IS A TABLE-SIDE FACT. "spirit and void damage caused by a haunt, spirit, or incorporeal undead" — whether an incoming packet came from a haunt/spirit/incorporeal undead is a per-attack determination the character sheet does not hold, exactly like every PF2e resistance the GM applies against a specific attacker. That is "something the printed text leaves to the table," explicitly not a defect. (The second printed sentence — "The first time you take damage from a haunt or spirit, you learn the general story of its origin" — is narrative with no sheet consequence.)

5. GREP RESULT. `the-dead-tell-tales` appears in exactly one place outside core.json: `scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:8903`, field `resistances`. No entry in featGrants.ts, featGrantsAuto.ts, featGrantsLane.ts, featPickGrants.ts, featFeatGrants.ts, featCantripGrants.ts, companionGrants.ts, situationalBonuses.ts, featUses.ts, domains.ts, modes.ts CATALOG_MODES, or casterArchetypes.ts — and none is needed, because the generic feat-resistance lane at derive.ts:2259 already reads it. `ourRegistries: []` in the packet is correct, not a gap.

RESIDUAL (not the claimed defect, not the proposed fix): the record carries no `condition` annotation, which would render a `*` on the pill (`DefensesPills.tsx:41`, `sources?.some((s) => s.condition)`) and print the clause in the breakdown (`explain.ts:1469`). That is a cosmetic display nicety shared by 253 of the 254 resistance entries in the corpus — it is not the "over-grant" alleged, and authoring `against` instead of `condition` is the one change that would turn a working record into a silent one.

rejected.summary: The named fireworks display the feat hands you is never added to the character — the `coughing-dragon` action record exists but nothing in core.json grants it, so it never appears in the encounter action list under its own name and its actual effect text is only reachable by clicking a description link.
why:
REFUTED — the player already receives the display, and the proposed fix as written would regress the record.

The claim's premise is that the feat hands the player nothing. But core.json feats['coughing-dragon-display'] carries actionCost {type:'actions', value:2} — the display's own printed cost — and that field IS read. src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:249 builds `actionRecords` from `...character.feats.map((f) => content.feats[f.featId])`; MainTab.tsx:277 filters it into `featActions` via `isActionCost(f.actionCost)` (defined MainTab.tsx:229, accepts type:'actions'); MainTab.tsx:1137-1142 renders that list under the "Feat actions" section of the encounter action list. ACTIVITIES in src/rules/actions.ts has no "Coughing Dragon" entry, so the `!activityNames.has(f.name)` guard does not drop it. A character with this feat gets a 2-action row on their turn.

The display's effect text is not stranded behind a dead link either. core-descriptions.json feats['coughing-dragon-display'].r = [{label:"Coughing Dragon", key:"actions"}]. The action row's popup renders at MainTab.tsx:759 `<DescBody description={a.fullDesc ?? a.desc} descRefs={a.fullRefs ?? a.descRefs} …/>`; the markdown branch (src/sheet/DescBody.tsx:110-120) resolves each ref through lookupRef (src/sheet/descref.ts:40), whose first candidate is map[slugify('Coughing Dragon')] = content.actions['coughing-dragon'] — which exists and holds the full "Choose either auditory or visual effects… counteract…" text.

The proposed fix is actively harmful as specified. featActions dedupes by NAME (MainTab.tsx:279, `seenActionNames`). "Coughing Dragon Display" and "Coughing Dragon" are different names, so authoring grantsActions:["coughing-dragon"] while the feat keeps its 2-action cost puts TWO 2-action rows on the sheet for one ability — the "offered the same thing twice" defect class, and exactly what scripts/nested-activate-check.mjs was written to catch (its header: a redundant copy "puts a passive feat in the encounter action list").

One honest residual, an attribution refinement rather than a missing mechanic: AoN feat-3246 prints `<actions string="" />` in its <title> (the Archives' way of saying passive) with a nested `**Coughing Dragon** <actions string="Two Actions" />`. The project's computed doctrine in scripts/nested-activate-check.mjs — if the granted activity ships as its own record the feat goes passive AND gains grantsActions; if it does not ship the feat keeps the nested cost — would prefer the paired form here, since content.actions['coughing-dragon'] does ship. That guard misses the four fireworks displays only because its regex requires `**Activate—X**` and these pages use a bare `**Coughing Dragon**` heading. But the change must be made as a PAIR (actionCost -> passive together with grantsActions) across all four display feats; the grant alone, which is what this claim proposes, converts a working single row into a duplicate. Nothing mechanical is lost today: neither route encodes the counteract modifier or rank as a number, so the player's outcome is identical — a 2-action activity on the sheet with the full text one tap away.

rejected.summary: The character is handed a Rage action card but no Rage state: there is no rage toggle to flip, so Rage's additional damage never exists and the feat's 2→4 upgrade has no base to raise.
why:
REFUTED — all three printed clauses have carriers with named readers, and the +4 is delivered as an absolute number that needs no engine-side rage base.

(1) "You can use the Rage action" — scripts/data/effect-backfill.json authors grantsActions:['rage'] (present on the record in public/core.json), read at src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:251-274, which puts a real Rage card in the encounter action list. The card carries the full Rage description from core-descriptions.json: temp HP = level + Con, "You deal 2 additional damage on melee Strikes", the agile halving, the concentrate restriction, the 1-minute duration.

(2) "While raging, you take a -1 penalty to AC" — src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2865 FEAT_SITUATIONAL['guards-fury'] entry {targets:[{kind:'ac'}], when:'while raging', bonus:'-1 (penalty)'}. Reached because characterSituationalIds seeds from c.feats.map(f=>f.featId) at src/rules/explain.ts:238; rendered because src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:298 gives Armor Class ref:{kind:'ac'}.

(3) "increase the additional damage from Rage from 2 to 4" — same registry line, second entry {targets:[{kind:'strikeDamage'}], when:'while raging and adjacent to your designated ally (melee & unarmed)', bonus:"+4 instead of Rage's +2"}. Rendered by src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:524 via statHasSituational(character,{kind:'strikeDamage',instanceId}) and openable from src/sheet/StrikeDetailModal.tsx:77.

WHERE THE CLAIM MISREADS: it treats the +4 as a delta requiring an engine +2 base ("no base to raise"). The star states the ABSOLUTE final number ("+4 instead of Rage's +2"), so no base is needed. Worse for the proposed fix: even with the suggested rage resource + derive.ts:3227 archetype extension, rageStrikeRider would emit +2, not +4 — RAGE_DAMAGE has no guards-fury row and archetype rage is flat 2 — so the toggle would not produce this feat's number; the star would still be the thing carrying it.

AND THE STAR IS THE CORRECT LANE, NOT A STOPGAP: the upgrade is conditional on "adjacent to your designated ally", live positional state about another character at the table that the engine has no representation for and can never resolve to a number. A conditional star is this project's sanctioned surfacing for exactly that, and the brief excludes clauses the star/note lanes already surface.

The claim's code reading is factually accurate (classResources.ts:108 gates rage on feat 'barbarian-dedication'; resourcesForCharacter at :208; derive.ts:3225-3228 returns null for non-barb/non-archetype; modes.ts:219 cat-rage is classes:['barbarian']), so a Guard's Fury character genuinely has no numeric rage toggle. But that is a request for deeper simulation of a state the printed text ties to table-level positioning — not a printed effect the player is denied. Every printed sentence reaches the sheet with the correct number.

rejected.summary: The player is asked "Difficult terrain" twice — once by this record and once by the Terrain Stalker it grants — and this record's own answer is read by nothing, so the two can disagree and only the granted feat's answer means anything.
why:
REFUTED. The claim's central assertion — "this record's own answer is read by nothing" — is false, and its conclusion is inverted in the exact case the printed sentence carves out.

1. THE READER EXISTS; the grep was the wrong instrument. The choice lane is shape-driven, not flag-driven — nothing in this codebase reads any feat `choice` by its flag string. The chain is: src/rules/build.ts:2874-2882 (`choiceKeys(slotKey, content.feats[featId]?.choice)` reads the answers out of `build.featChoices` and writes `featChoiceById[slotKey] = {value,label}`) -> src/rules/build.ts:3747 (`feats.push({ featId, level: lvl, category, choice: featChoiceById[slotKey], slotKey })`) -> src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:112 (`name: (fc.choice ? `${feat.name} (${fc.choice.label})` : feat.name) + pickSuffix(...)`). The answer renders on the Feats tab as "Underbrush Trailblazer (Snow)". The identical grep test applied to Terrain Stalker's own flag ('choice') would equally "prove" ITS answer is read by nothing, which is obviously false.

2. THE CLAIM IS INVERTED IN THE PRINTED FALLBACK CASE. build.ts:3965 `if (takenFeats.has(gid) && !distinctTaking) continue;`, with `distinctTaking` true only for `fixedLore` bindings (build.ts:3962). Slot-picked feats enter `takenFeats` at build.ts:3744, before the grant loop. So for a character who ALREADY HAS Terrain Stalker — exactly the printed condition "if you already have Terrain Stalker for underbrush, you can select a different type of difficult terrain" — the grant is deduped, no second Terrain Stalker row is pushed, and `grantedChoiceById['terrain-stalker']` (the answer to the granted picker at Builder.tsx:2076) reaches nothing at all. This record's own `choice` is the ONLY surviving carrier of the printed fallback terrain. It is the granted picker that goes dead in that branch, not this record's choice.

3. THE SIBLING ARGUMENT COLLAPSES ON THE PRINTED TEXT. silent-stone prints "you gain the Terrain Stalker skill feat" and pack-stalker "You gain the Terrain Stalker feat" — neither names a terrain nor carries a fallback clause, so both correctly carry no own choice. terrain-scout grants twice. underbrush-trailblazer is the only one of the four whose own sentence contains a per-record terrain decision. The asymmetry is printed, not accidental.

4. THE PROPOSED FIX WOULD DELETE PRINTED CONTENT. Dropping the `choice` removes the only store for the fallback terrain. And FEAT_GRANT_BOUND_CHOICE cannot express this binding: boundGrantChoice (src/rules/build.ts:1371-1396) has four kinds — fixed / fixedLore / skillChoice / loreChoice — and none reads `build.featChoices`; skillChoice/loreChoice index FEAT_GRANTS slots. `kind:'fixed', skill:'underbrush'` would hard-bind underbrush and erase the "you can select a different type of difficult terrain" branch.

Honest residual (NOT the claimed defect): when the player does not already have Terrain Stalker, both prompts render on the same card (Builder.tsx:1913-1925 for the record's own, Builder.tsx:2076 for the granted). That is a labelling wart deserving a `note` like terrain-scout's, but no answer is lost, both display, and the proposed fix would remove printed content rather than fix it.
